Definition: to wilt; generally, to fall away, fail, faint; figuratively, to be foolish or (morally) wicked; causatively, to despise, disgrace
BiblicalUsage: 1) to be senseless, be foolish; 1a) (Qal) to be foolish; 1b) (Piel); 1b1) to regard or treat as foolish; 1b2) to treat with contempt; 2) to sink or drop down, languish, wither and fall, fade; 2a) (Qal); 2a1) to sink or drop down; 2a2) to fall, wither and fall, fade; 2a3) to droop
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
